name: Railway
description: Every backend (Railpack or Dockerfile), Next.js, static SPAs in a container, and Railway Postgres.

specSections.title: Environments & Configuration
specSections.guidance: Per environment (production on main; preview = the aide-preview environment): each service's root directory, Dockerfile, health path, pre-deploy migrate command and domain, the database (Railway Postgres, DATABASE_URL = ${{Postgres.DATABASE_URL}}), every env var, and the origin model (same-origin SPA container proxying over the private network, or cross-origin). Note Railway Free/Trial limits.

requiredEnv.description: The backend's private-network URL (e.g. http://api.railway.internal:8080) that the SPA container's nginx proxies /api/ to (same-origin on Railway, FR-146).
requiredEnv.when: originModel == same-origin && frontendHost == deploy-railway && backendHost == deploy-railway

checklist.item: Each service has a multi-stage Dockerfile with a non-root USER and a .dockerignore, and listens on $PORT on IPv4 and IPv6
The image contains the data pack's one-off migrate command for the pre-deploy
The backend's ready health path exists and checks the database
The backend handles Railway's postgresql:// DATABASE_URL reference
Same-origin SPA: nginx proxies /api/ to API_ORIGIN over the private network, re-resolving railway.internal
Any .railway/railway.ts is marked as documentation; no legacy railway.json or railway.toml and no literal secrets
No CI job, script or package script deploys with the Railway CLI; AIDE triggers every deploy
.env.example lists every variable the app needs, with placeholders only
